A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ASFT study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material across the reorganized appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original mathematical reasoning, medical QA, and code-generation experiments, alongside ablations, model-scaling results, and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds an alternative-anchoring comparison, with revised KL-direction and LoRA findings.

M1.justification: Equation (6) changes the specified anchoring loss from KL(policy || base) to KL(base || policy), and Section 5.3 explicitly switches the selected direction from reverse to forward KL. Section 6.6 also introduces ASFT-SFT, combining DFT with an SFT-loss penalty. The PDFs do not establish whether the retained experiments were rerun.

E1.justification: Both versions retain NuminaMath training and the same five math benchmarks, MedMCQA training and the same medical benchmarks, and Magicoder training with HumanEval/MBPP evaluations. The new anchoring comparison reuses math and medical tasks; continual learning is proposed only as future work.

E2.justification: Section 6.6 newly evaluates ASFT-SFT against KL-anchored ASFT, alongside Base, SFT, and DFT reference curves. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new alternative-anchoring experiment introduces an alpha sweep over 0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.5, 1, 5, and 10. Existing benchmark data scales, model sizes, training budgets, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. The newly specified LoRA learning rate is disclosure; v1 provides no LoRA-specific rate establishing a setting change.

E4.justification: Section 6.6 and the new Figure 4 test whether SFT loss can replace KL anchoring across math and medical tasks. The KL-direction ablation in Section 5.3/Figure 2 is substantively revised. Conversely, v1's Appendix F.2 token-probability distribution analysis is removed; model-scaling and hyperparameter analyses remain in reorganized appendices.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging mathematical reasoning accuracy over 16 decoding runs and otherwise retain point-estimate reporting. No new seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are documented.

E6.justification: The central KL-direction finding reverses: Section 5.3/Figure 2 favors reverse KL in v1 and forward KL in v3. Table 4 replaces LoRA accuracy/time of 34.32/0.562 hours with 39.45/0.594 hours; this is not an established same-setting gain because v1 omits its LoRA learning rate. Alternative-anchor results are added and the token histogram removed, while benchmark scores in Tables 1–3 and 5 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix D.2 introduces the Frozen-q Surrogate lemma and proof explaining why stop-gradient makes dropped terms constant within each update. The generalized derivation now explicitly requires fixed q. Proposition 1 and the strict-tightness covariance proof are retained, with the latter moved from Appendix E to D.4.

C1.justification: The abstract, three stated contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: DFT provides tighter RL bounds but suffers drift, and KL-anchored ASFT improves stability and performance across reasoning, medical knowledge, and code generation with modest overhead.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanation reverses: forward KL's mode-covering behavior changes from a disadvantage to the reason anchoring prevents collapse, while reverse KL is criticized for mode seeking. The introduction and Section 4.1 replace threatened bound validity with deteriorating tightness and increased weight variance. Section 6.6 and expanded limitations add substantive discussion of base-model priors and domain-dependent anchoring trade-offs.

D1.justification: Code availability changes from a promised release to a reported completed release. Section 6.5 newly specifies the ASFT-LoRA learning rate as 5e-4 while retaining rank 8. Hardware and principal training details remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify repository availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hu et al. (2021) on LoRA to support its discussion of adaptation and learning-rate selection. The related-work section and positioning relative to SFT, RL, and importance-weighted approaches otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 removes duplicated introductory prose, corrects wording and headings, and updates affiliations and publication headers. It adds Section 6.6 and post-conclusion material and consolidates the theoretical and experimental appendices. Most existing prose and the main narrative remain intact; the original Appendix B limitations also remain.

P2.justification: Results presentation is broadly redesigned: Tables 1–3 and 5 receive revised grouping, typography, and arrow-coded differences. Figures 2 and 5 are redrawn with changed styling and axes. The token-distribution Figure 4 is removed and a new anchoring-comparison Figure 4 added, alongside substantial appendix reflow.

improvement.justification: The frozen-q lemma clarifies a previously implicit condition in the derivation, and the alternative-anchor ablation strengthens examination of the KL design choice. LoRA hyperparameter disclosure and reported code release also improve reproducibility information. These targeted gains are tempered by the unexplained KL-direction reversal and a new inconsistency: Section 6.5 reports 13.4% LoRA overhead, while the limitations retain 7.3%.
